B01.evidence: Two pale closed loops meet at the one heavy vertex; their further crossing is unmarked. Both readings preserve this incidence. Different curve control points and filled-vertex contours alone do not establish another material difference.

B02.evidence: Five pairs of dark endpoints are visible. The first three have joining strokes; in the fourth, short faint upper and lower stubs survive but the middle is not joined. The fifth pair has no connecting line. The upper endpoint of the first pair has a small pale center. The second tracing captures these visible details without completing the fourth connector.

B03.evidence: Six heavy points, overlapping outer traces, and the long left-to-right inner chord are visible. A further faint run curves down from the upper-right vertex inside the right contour and bends left toward the lowest vertex. The first drawing lacked part of this run. Its visible portions are added, with breaks where the hatching obscures continuity; the whole figure retains its existing uncertainty about faint incidence. The second reader also recognized the curved run. Lower retraced arcs are retained without interpreting every crossing as a vertex.

B04.evidence: The heavy two-point edge, two small endpoint enclosures, broad surrounding curve, left continuation and three rays from the right point are visible. The broad enclosure and right small enclosure have gaps. The first tracing preserves them; the second closes the broad outline. No arrows or labels are supplied.

B05.evidence: The broad oval and left small endpoint enclosure have visible upper/side gaps. The central heavy connection has a closely retraced pale band. The first approximation retains the gaps and retracing, while the second regularizes the enclosing paths as closed. No extra independent graph edge is inferred from the broad band.
